result.audit_summary: Security audit of the Agent module completed. Found 8 issues: 3 critical, 2 high, 2 medium, 1 low. 5 issues were fixed.

issues.title: Code injection vulnerability in CalculatorTool using eval() - FIXED
issues.description: The CalculatorTool used Python's eval() function with user-supplied input. Although builtins were blocked, attackers could still use type introspection to bypass restrictions (e.g., eval("().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()") to access dangerous classes).
issues.impact: Remote code execution possible through math expression input
issues.fix_applied: Replaced eval() with AST-based safe evaluation using ast.parse() and compile(). Added whitelist of allowed math functions (abs, round, min, max, sum, pow, divmod) and constants (pi, e, tau, inf). Validates result is numeric type before returning.

issues.title: Missing authorization check in debug_history action - FIXED
issues.description: The debug_history action's DELETE method did not verify that the agent belongs to the requesting user before clearing debug history. Users could potentially delete debug history for agents they don't own.
issues.impact: Users could delete debug history for agents they don't own
issues.fix_applied: Added explicit owner verification: AgentExecution.objects.filter(agent__owner=request.user, agent=agent) ensures users can only access/delete their own data.

issues.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in WebScraperTool
issues.description: The WebScraperTool accepts any URL without validation. Attackers could use the agent to scan internal services (localhost, 127.0.0.1, internal IPs), access cloud metadata endpoints, or probe internal network infrastructure.
issues.impact: Internal network reconnaissance and potential access to sensitive internal services
issues.fix_recommended: Add URL validation to reject private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), localhost, and cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254). Use a whitelist of allowed domains if possible.

issues.title: Potential mass assignment in AgentSerializer
issues.description: The serializer includes 'settings' field which could allow users to set sensitive fields like api_key through the settings JSON. Additionally, 'tools' and 'skills' fields are directly exposed.
issues.impact: Users could potentially modify fields they shouldn't have access to
issues.fix_recommended: Review serializer fields. Consider moving 'settings' and potentially sensitive fields to read-only or excluding them from regular serializers. Add explicit validation for 'tools' and 'skills' to ensure only valid tool names are accepted.

issues.title: System prompt and user input directly passed to LLM without sanitization
issues.description: User-controlled messages are directly passed to the LLM without sanitization. While this is expected for AI agents, malicious prompts could potentially manipulate agent behavior or extract conversation history.
issues.impact: Prompt injection attacks could manipulate agent behavior or leak conversation data
issues.fix_recommended: Implement input filtering for known prompt injection patterns. Consider adding instruction boundaries or separators. Monitor for common injection techniques.

issues.title: CORS configured with credentials and multiple origins
issues.description: CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS is set to True with origins from environment variable. While origins are configurable, the combination of credentials and multiple origins requires careful validation to prevent credential leakage.
issues.impact: If ALLOWED_HOSTS or CORS_ORIGINS is misconfigured, credentials could be sent to unauthorized origins
issues.fix_recommended: Ensure CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is properly configured in production. Consider using CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS_REGEXES for more flexible validation. Add validation that CORS_ORIGINS and ALLOWED_HOSTS are properly set in production.

issues.title: No rate limiting on chat endpoints
issues.description: The chat and stream_chat endpoints handle potentially expensive LLM calls but don't have specific rate limiting. The global DRF throttle is in place but may not be sufficient for LLM usage control.
issues.impact: Users could exhaust LLM quotas or incur excessive costs
issues.fix_recommended: Consider adding specific rate limits for chat endpoints, potentially based on agent or user tier. Track usage for billing purposes.

issues.title: Error messages may leak implementation details
issues.description: In several places, exception messages are returned to users or logged with full stack traces. While not critical, detailed error messages could aid attackers in understanding the system.
issues.impact: Attackers could gain insight into system internals through error messages
issues.fix_recommended: Ensure error handlers return sanitized messages to users while detailed logs are kept server-side.

positive_findings.description: All Agent endpoints have IsAuthenticated permission class properly applied
get_queryset() properly filters agents by owner in AgentViewSet and AgentConversationViewSet
AgentExecutionViewSet and AgentToolViewSet properly filter by agent__owner
Chat endpoints validate message is not empty before processing
Role validation in add_message action restricts to 'user', 'assistant', 'system'
Django CSRF middleware is enabled globally
X-Frame-Options middleware is enabled to prevent clickjacking
No raw SQL queries found; all database operations use Django ORM with proper parameterization
No file upload functionality in Agent module
API keys are read from environment variables, not hardcoded
Token-based authentication is configured alongside JWT

security_score.notes: Score reflects post-fix status. 2 critical issues were fixed during audit. 5 issues documented for future improvement (SSRF, mass assignment, prompt injection, CORS, rate limiting).

summary: Security audit completed. Found 8 issues: 3 critical, 2 high, 2 medium, 1 low. Fixed 2 critical issues: (1) Code injection in CalculatorTool - replaced eval() with AST-based safe evaluation using ast.parse() with whitelist of allowed functions/constants; (2) Authorization bypass in debug_history - added explicit agent__owner filtering. 5 issues documented for future improvement (SSRF in web scraper, mass assignment in serializer, prompt injection, CORS configuration, rate limiting). All endpoints properly authenticated with IsAuthenticated. No SQL injection found.
